_notes: Taito do Brasil, 1981-85 firmware (four 2KB ROMs; Mr. Black has five). Compiled 2026-10 by evilwraith from the
Vortex ROM and live NVRAM captures on an AtGames ALP4K (Visual Pinball Standalone).
Evidence per set: vortex and mrblack - a full live game each read back its final score and credits exactly;
sharkt, cosmic, stest - a saved attract image each (high score, settings, display); every other set listed -
its ROM code references every declared address in the same way (settings copy to 0x4070, high-score compare at
0x4079, credits copy 0x407F to 0x408D, the replay routine, the game-over write), with no image yet.
Display scores are three BCD bytes least-significant first (platform endian: little); 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF is a blank
display. The nine-byte BCD settings block is edited from the service menu and validated at reset (a non-BCD byte
restores all nine from ROM); its nine entries are identified from the Shock operator sheet (see adjustments).
No checksum. The firmware deliberately resumes a game in progress at reset; PinMAME's taito driver (2026-10)
marks the saved game over on load so a table starts in attract.
0x40F4-0x40FF holds the last game's final display (four scores, same encoding as 0x4080) once the game is over, while the attract alternates the live display between it and the high score.

Audits are the eight 16-bit little-endian binary counters at +50..+5F that the firmware's statistics display walks two bytes at a time (Vortex 0x08BB). Four are identified from live captures; +50, +58, +5A and +5E read zero in every capture and are not declared.

player_count._notes: Read by the reset path, which refuses to resume a game with a value of 5 or more; 1 throughout a live one-player game, 0 in attract.
player_count.label: Players

current_player._notes: One bit per player - 1, 2, 4, 8 for players one to four, 0 in attract - which the values list turns into the player number. The firmware finds the number by rotating the byte right until the carry sets and compares it with the player count (Vortex 0x0445). Measured as 1 in one-player games; the multi-player values are from the code.
current_player.label: Current Player

credits._notes: Stored value; the firmware keeps a display copy at 0x408D.
credits.label: Credits

match._notes: Match digit shown after the game; cycles 0-9 during play (the randomiser).
match.label: Match

game_over._notes: Bit 0 of the firmware's flags byte: set in attract and by its reset path when it declines to resume, clear during a game.
game_over.label: Game Over

tilted._notes: Bit 1 of the flags byte: set at a tilt on ball 1 and cleared when the next ball started (live on Vortex).
tilted.label: Tilted

score._notes: Most-significant byte first, unlike the display; the reset path reloads it from the ROM's minimum if it reads lower.

01._notes: Labels and ranges from the Shock (1979) and Cosmic (1981) operator sheets in backport/Manuals; byte positions and defaults match every image captured (Cosmic's default column is its image byte for byte). Defaults are each set's own factory table, read from its ROM (the ten bytes the reset path copies in when a settings byte is not BCD).
01.label: Balls Per Game

02._notes: 'Fichas/Partida' (Cosmic: 'Credito/Partida'). A two-digit code, not a count: the sheets allow 11-14 and list 15 as a forbidden value that forces the default. What the digits mean is not stated on either sheet.
02.label: Coinage (code)

03._notes: 'Credito/Maximo'. The firmware clamps the stored credits to this value at boot.
03.label: Maximum Credits

04._notes: 'Incentivo'; the sheet allows 01 and 11-14. The 1980 games (drakor, meteort) hold 04 here, outside that set, so its meaning on those is not confirmed.
04.label: Incentive

05._notes: '1o Score'. Shown x10,000 (the map's scale; min/max are in those units, as upstream does). One BCD byte compared against the two most-significant digits of the score (x10,000); the same routine in every set. On Cosmic (and likely this generation) CODE switches 5-7 select the level from a fixed table and the firmware copies it into this byte at every game start, so an edit here does not outlast the next game while those switches are raised.
05.label: Replay Level 1

06._notes: Shown x10,000. '2o Score'. Annulled when equal to adjustment 5 (the sheet says so, and the routine skips it). On Cosmic (and likely this generation) CODE switches 5-7 select the level from a fixed table and the firmware copies it into this byte at every game start, so an edit here does not outlast the next game while those switches are raised.
06.label: Replay Level 2

07._notes: Named from the Shock and Cosmic operator sheets. The firmware compares the score with this level and, unless it equals replay level 2, jumps to a per-game hook; the hook does something game-specific on cavnegro, cavnegr1, cavnegr2; returns immediately - the setting has no effect - on vortex, mrblack, sharkt, cosmic, stest, fireactd, gork, hawkman, hawkman1, ladylukt, lunelle, mrblack1, polar, rally, snake, sshuttle, sshuttl1, titan, titan1, vegast, voleybal, zarza, zarza1, gemini, sureshot, gemini1. Read from each ROM's code.
07.label: Extra Ball Score

09._notes: 'Credito/Record': credits awarded for beating the high score.
09.label: Credits For High Score

01._notes: Ticks only while a game is running (live on Drakor and Oba-Oba), about every 64 s like the powered-on timer. The statistics display divides it by games played for an average game time.
01.label: Play Time (ticks)

02._notes: Ticks about every 64 s whether or not a game is running (Vortex in attract: 44, 108, 173, 237, 301 s).
02.label: Powered-On Time (ticks)

03._notes: One tick per coin, on the same poll the credit rose, in all five live captures (2, 2, 3, 3 and 2 coins).
03.label: Coins

04._notes: Ticks at game start, with ball 0->1 and the credit consumed, in all five live captures.
04.label: Games Played
